title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
description:
Given a binary search tree (BST), find the **lowest common ancestor (LCA)** node of two given nodes `p` and `q` in the BST.

The lowest common ancestor is defined between two nodes `p` and `q` as the lowest node in the tree `T` that has both `p` and `q` as descendants (where we allow **a node to be a descendant of itself**).

Your method receives the `root` of the BST along with references to the two target nodes `p` and `q`, and must return the `TreeNode` reference to their LCA in the tree. In test inputs, `p` and `q` are shown by their unique node values, and the output shows the LCA node's value.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 10^5].
p and q will exist in the BST.
hints: Use the BST ordering property: if both p.val and q.val are strictly smaller than cur.val, the LCA must lie in cur.left.
If both p.val and q.val are strictly greater than cur.val, the LCA must lie in cur.right.
The first node where p and q split to different sides—or where cur equals p or q—is the lowest common ancestor.

examples.explanation: Nodes 2 and 8 lie in the left and right subtrees of 6 respectively, so their LCA is 6.
Node 4 is in the right subtree of 2, and a node is a descendant of itself, so the LCA of 2 and 4 is 2.
Node 1 is the left child of root 2, so the LCA of 2 and 1 is 2.

inputs.name: p
inputs.description: Value of the first target node

inputs.name: q
inputs.description: Value of the second target node
